p: Once the novelty of the first session wears off, karting gets properly addictive. That's because the lap times don't lie. Beat your mates once and it's fun; knock half a second off your own best and you're hooked.

A few things make a real difference. Work out where the braking points are and use the same marker every lap. Keep your steering smooth, because sawing at the wheel slows the kart down. And don't get rattled when someone's right on your bumper. Hold your line, drive your own race and let them make the mistakes.
It's worth knowing that karting is more physical than it looks. Your forearms and shoulders will feel it, especially on a twisty track, so keep your grip relaxed and breathe on the straights.

Keep your expectations realistic on your first visit. Seasoned karters have spent hours learning a track, so don't be disheartened if their times are well ahead. Just focus on beating your own last lap.

For a calmer finish to the day, Lister Park is home to Cartwright Hall art gallery and its lovely gardens, and City Park in the centre has its big mirror pool and fountains, which the kids will happily splash about in on a warm day. Then there's the curry, of course. Bradford doesn't do small portions.
